pages.alt: Mia, Tavi and Sol stand beside the library table and the finished map from their first adventure.

pages.text:
The parcel from the end of the first mystery was waiting in the library. It had slid down the wall ramp and stopped beside the five-star map.

The label showed three names: MIA, SOL AND TAVI.
pages.subtext: The friends gathered around their parcel to see what was inside.
pages.alt: The labelled parcel that slid down the library ramp waits beside the five-star map. Mia, Sol and Tavi gather around it.

pages.text:
Mia opened the parcel. Inside was a round Moon Lantern and a card.

The card said: PLEASE TAKE THIS LANTERN TO THE BALCONY BEFORE THE FIRST EVENING STAR.
pages.subtext: The picture on the card showed where to take it.
pages.alt: The open parcel holds a round Moon Lantern. A simple picture card points to the balcony.

pages.text:
The friends carried the lantern towards the balcony. A small door blocked the way. The lantern was too wide to go through the door.

Pax came over. “Hello! I’m Pax. I know how to help.”
pages.subtext: The team’s question: How can the whole lantern get through the small door?
pages.alt: Pax greets the team beside a small doorway. The round lantern is clearly wider than the opening.

pages.text:
“We can take the lantern apart,” said Pax. “Then carry every part through the door. Then put the whole lantern together again.”

First, they looked closely at the lantern.
pages.subtext: Their plan: check the whole, count every part, carry every part, then rebuild the whole.
pages.alt: Pax shows the team a simple four-step picture plan beside the whole Moon Lantern.

pages.badge: TRY IT · FIND THE WHOLE LANTERN
pages.text:
Look at all three pictures.

One lantern has a gap. One has every part. One has an extra shape.

Which one is the whole lantern?
pages.subtext: Choose before you turn the page.
pages.alt: The first lantern has a gap. The second is round with every part. The third has an extra triangle attached.

pages.text:
WHOLE LANTERN.
NO GAP. NO EXTRA PIECE.

“This is the whole lantern,” said Pax. “Every part of this lantern is here.”
pages.subtext: Whole means every part is here. No part is missing, and no extra part has been added. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: The round Moon Lantern fills its tray and is labelled whole, with no gap and no extra shape.

pages.text:
Pax placed four glowing spots on the floor. Each spot stood for one lantern part.

“We must check every spot,” said Mia. “Then no part will be left behind.”
pages.subtext: The four spots help the team keep track of every part.
pages.alt: Four glowing carrying spots make one clear row on the floor.

pages.text:
Point to the four glowing spots, one after another.

Touch each spot once. Do not miss one. Do not touch one twice.
pages.subtext: This is how the team will keep track of all four lantern parts.
pages.alt: Four large separate glowing spots wait in one row for the child to point to each once.

pages.text:
ONE · TWO · THREE · FOUR.

Each spot was touched once. None was missed. None was touched twice.
pages.subtext: The team can use the same check when they carry the four lantern parts. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: The four spots each show one footprint, with no empty spot and no spot carrying two footprints.

pages.text:
Sol checked the spots: “One, two, three, three, four!”

His count did not match the four spots. What did Sol do?
pages.subtext: Look at the footprints on every spot before you turn.
pages.alt: The four carrying spots show one footprint on spots one, two and four, but two footprints on spot three.

pages.text:
SPOT THREE WAS TOUCHED TWICE.

“The footprints show us what happened,” said Tavi.
pages.subtext: Sol tried again and touched every spot once. Now his count matched the four parts. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: One picture shows two footprints on spot three. A second picture shows one footprint on every spot.

pages.text:
Now the team was ready to choose how to take the lantern apart.

Pax showed three plans. “We need four same-size pieces that meet in the middle and fill the whole circle.”
pages.subtext: The right plan will make four clear parts to carry through the small door.
pages.alt: Pax shows three clear plans for taking the round lantern apart.

pages.text:
Which picture shows four same-size pieces that meet in the middle and fill the circle?

Check that there is no gap and no piece is over another piece.
pages.subtext: Point to one picture before you turn.
pages.alt: One picture has a gap. In one, pieces cover each other. One fills the circle with four symmetrical same-size pieces.

pages.text:
Trace around each circle. Does a piece leave a gap?

Look from left to right. Do the sides match?
Look from top to bottom. Do those sides match too?
pages.subtext: Matching sides around the middle are called symmetrical. Check each picture before you choose.
pages.alt: The three choices stay visible while the child checks for a gap, overlap and matching symmetrical sides.

pages.text:
NO GAP.
NO PIECE OVER ANOTHER.
FOUR PIECES THE SAME SIZE.
LEFT AND RIGHT MATCH. TOP AND BOTTOM MATCH.

“That balanced match is called symmetrical,” said Pax.
pages.subtext: Together, the four parts meet in the middle and fill the same whole circle. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: Four same-size symmetrical pieces meet in the middle and fill the circle without covering each other.

pages.text:
Pax used the four-part plan. The lantern came apart into four pieces.

The four parts landed in four clear spaces. Each part was small enough to fit through the door.
pages.subtext: The team can see all four lantern parts before they move them.
pages.alt: Four same-size lantern parts sit in four clear spaces beside the small door.

pages.text:
Move all four lantern parts through the small door.

Use each carrying spot once. Leave no lantern part behind.
pages.subtext: Count the parts as they go through: one, two, three, four.
pages.alt: Four coloured lantern parts wait on one side of a small door, with four matching spaces on the other side.

pages.text:
ONE · TWO · THREE · FOUR.

All four lantern parts were on the other side. No part was left behind.
pages.subtext: Next, the team will check and count the four parts before the final rebuild. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: All four lantern parts sit in four clear spaces on the far side of the small door.

pages.text:
Before rebuilding the lantern, Pax checked the pieces against the plan.

Which pair has two pieces that are the same size: Pair A or Pair B?
pages.subtext: Look at both pieces in each pair before you turn.
pages.alt: Pair A has two pieces of the same size. Pair B has one big piece and one small piece.

pages.text:
PAIR A: EQUAL IN SIZE.
PAIR B: NOT EQUAL IN SIZE.

“Both pieces in Pair A are the same size,” said Pax. “They are equal in size.”
pages.subtext: One piece in Pair B is bigger than the other.
pages.alt: Pair A is equal in size. Pair B has one big piece and one small piece.

pages.text:
On the other side of the small door, Pax put three lantern parts into a flat practice frame. One of its four spaces was still empty.

“Does this practice picture show all four parts?” asked Sol.
pages.subtext: Look at all four spaces. Decide before you turn.
pages.alt: A flat practice frame has four spaces. Three hold lantern parts and one space is empty.

pages.text:
ONE SPACE IS EMPTY.
THE PRACTICE PICTURE DOES NOT SHOW ALL FOUR PARTS YET.

“We still need one more part,” said Mia.
pages.subtext: Pax placed the fourth part in the practice frame, checked it, then returned all four parts to the carrying tray.
pages.alt: The fourth part fills the practice-frame gap. After the check, all four parts return to the tray.

pages.text:
A loose triangle from Pax’s work table slid beside the four lantern parts.

“The four lantern parts are already here,” said Tavi. “This triangle does not belong to the lantern.”
pages.subtext: The triangle is extra. It stays outside the carrying tray. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: All four lantern parts are on the tray. A loose triangle from Pax's table stays outside.

pages.text:
Before they carried the four separate parts to the balcony, Pax held two of them. The other two waited on the tray.

How many parts is Pax holding?
How many parts make the whole lantern?
pages.subtext: Look at Pax’s hands and all four parts. Say both numbers before you turn.
pages.alt: Pax holds two lantern parts while the other two wait on the tray, so all four remain visible.

pages.text:
PAX IS HOLDING TWO PIECES.
FOUR PIECES MAKE THE WHOLE LANTERN.

“Two tells us what I am holding in the picture. Four tells us how many make the whole lantern,” said Pax.
pages.subtext: Say both numbers again. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: Labels on Pax's practice picture show the two pieces held and the four pieces that make the whole lantern.

pages.text:
At the balcony, the four lantern parts were still separate. Pax put one part in each counting space.

1 PART + 1 PART + 1 PART + 1 PART = ? PARTS

Is the total 3, 4 or 5?
pages.subtext: Touch each lantern part once. Then choose the total that names every visible part.
pages.alt: Four separate same-size lantern parts sit in four counting spaces. A plus sign is between each space. The equation ends with an equals sign and a question mark.

pages.text:
1 PART + 1 PART + 1 PART + 1 PART = 4 PARTS

The PLUS signs join the separate counted parts.
The EQUALS sign says both sides count the same four parts.
pages.subtext: Nothing was lost, repeated or added. Both sides name the same total.
pages.alt: The equation one part plus one part plus one part plus one part equals four parts appears above the same four visible lantern parts.

pages.text:
The equation counted FOUR SEPARATE PARTS.

Now the friends fitted those four parts together. The same Moon Lantern was ONE WHOLE again.
pages.subtext: 4 PARTS → 1 WHOLE LANTERN. This arrow shows rebuilding. It is not an equals sign.
pages.alt: Four separate lantern parts point towards the same parts fitted together as one whole Moon Lantern.

pages.text:
1. Count every visible part once.
2. 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4 PARTS.
3. PLUS joins separate counts. EQUALS says both sides have the same total.
4. Those 4 parts can fit together to rebuild 1 whole lantern.
pages.subtext: Say both ideas: four parts altogether; those four parts rebuild one whole.
pages.alt: Pax shows the four-part addition equation beside a picture of four parts being rebuilt as one whole lantern.

pages.text:
The lantern lit up as the first evening star appeared.

A blue moon picture shone. Then a gold sun picture shone. Then the blue moon came back.
pages.subtext: The pictures were taking turns. Next: Book E03 · The Fold Makes a Pattern
pages.alt: The whole Moon Lantern glows beneath one evening star. A blue moon picture and a gold sun picture take turns across its round face.
